newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: India wool tariff cut seen helping Australia sales.
newsitem.headline: India wool tariff cut seen helping Australia sales.

text.p: The Australian government on Friday welcomed significant cuts to import duties on apparel wool recently introduced by the Indian government.
Primary Industries Minister John Anderson said the tariff on imports of raw apparel wool, greasy, scoured and carbonised, had been cut to 20 percent from 25 percent.
The tariff on wool tops had been reduced to 40 percent from 50 percent.
A temporary additional surcharge of two percent applies to the products, giving effective rates of 22 percent and 42 percent respectively.
"This outcome highlights the value of the government's bilateral approach to market access," Anderson said.
"During his recent visit to Australia, I had a very positive discussion with the Indian Textiles Minister regarding the benefits for both our countries of a partnership in wool."
Anderson said the tariff cuts would boost Australian wool sales and provide better access to the Indian domestic clothing market.

The International Wool Secretariat estimates that between 1994 and 2005 the volume of apparel wool consumed by Indian mills would increase by a minimum of 130 percent, to 55 million kilograms in 2005 fr5om 24 million kg in 1994.
The Indian industry is more optimistic, forecasting a 200 percent rise to 73 million kg over the same period, Anderson said.
India is Australia's tenth largest market for wool.
